facts.fact: Matin Libre reports Parakou has full cadastral coverage with 196,474 parcels registered in the national cadastre on the e-Foncier Bénin platform, with over 11,500 registration certificates (CEC) distributed by 1 September 2026.

Municipal officials say cadastral data updating continues and new e-Foncier Bénin functions for recasement attestations, mutation certificates and compulsions are to be developed, while the PPMEC project aims for a complete cadastre.

Fraternité reports 445,695 parcels registered in the national cadastre on the ANDF-run e-Foncier Bénin platform, covering 24 arrondissements in 12 communes, with Cotonou fully covered and CEC issuance effective in all 12 communes.

Fraternité reports the PPMEC project (July 2023 to June 2026) is preparing nationwide scale-up of the cadastre, with Parakou and Porto-Novo coverage being finalised and extension under way in further localities.

facts.fact: Benin's government says PPMEC II (2026-2031, 12 communes) continues cadastral data collection and TERRA BENIN (14 communes first) aims to register 1.5 million parcels, both launched on 6 November 2026.

MDF says e-Foncier Benin records land rights for part of the country, with 491,293 parcels mapped, 222,463 people with recorded rights and 2 municipalities and 387 villages almost fully registered in 2021-2025, and a national cadastre for all 77 communes is the aim.

ANDF says e-Foncier Bénin, built on the LADM standard, records parcels titled or not, and cadastral data collection has covered Cotonou, Porto-Novo and Parakou fully and nine other communes in part, while ANDF digitised all the physical files inherited from the former land directorate.
ANDF says E-TERRE is connected to the National Public Services Portal so users can carry out certain land procedures online.
